title: C05 — Detailed design of reservation approval

blocks.content: We design teacher approval of a reservation in ReservationService.approve, within the reservation management responsibility from C03. The operation changes a pending request to confirmed and records its history and a student notification.

rows: Teachers approve requests for their own consultation slots.
The actor's identity comes from an authenticated session.
A slot has at most one active reservation; both PENDING and CONFIRMED block it.

blocks.content: Design intent: ReservationService decides authorization and the permitted state transition. Checks precede mutation; identity and role checks also precede loading the reservation. State, history and notification must be persisted together or not at all. These rules define the intended implementation and verification.
Scope: PENDING → CONFIRMED. Creation and cancellation have separate rules. Some implementation already exists; its consistency with this design is assessed in the evidence below.

rows: D1: Check the authenticated actor and active role
Unauthenticated users and students must not approve or discover reservation existence through this operation.
D2: Validate input and load the reservation and teacher
Distinguish invalid input from a missing record.
D3: Check slot ownership and pending state
Only the owner may approve, and only from PENDING.
D4: Confirm the reservation and record the time
The resulting state and confirmation time must be explicit.
Record who approved and inform the student.
D6: Persist atomically and propagate errors
A partially persisted change must not be reported as success.

Identity, active role, ID, reservation state
Rules apply to every service caller, not only the HTTP controller.

blocks.content: approve takes a reservation ID, trusted identity and a request with an optional note. Authentication creates the identity; the service does not validate the token itself. Success conditions and failures are defined in section 6.
findById requires a non-null ID. It returns the reservation or Optional.empty when absent. Database errors propagate. It does not guarantee exclusive locking.

blocks.content: Success invariants: reservation ID, student and slot stay unchanged. Approval does not release the slot: PENDING and CONFIRMED are active. History records action CONFIRMED, transition PENDING → CONFIRMED and the authenticated teacher. A null note is valid. Repeated approval returns a conflict.

Failure contract: validation and authorization errors occur before mutation. A technical failure after confirm() may alter the in-memory object but must leave no confirmed reservation or new history/notification in the database. This requires a call through Spring's transaction proxy with all writes participating in the same transaction. Direct unit-test calls do not prove rollback. Status codes here describe ApiException; HTTP filters or validation may reject requests earlier.
Persistence: JPA dirty checking writes changes to the managed entity when the transaction completes, so approve need not call reservations.save. Internal notifications use the same database.

Concurrency: this design does not yet ensure that simultaneous approvals produce only one history record and notification. The active-reservation unique index does not solve this problem. Concurrency protection remains an open design risk.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as ReservationController
    participant S as ReservationService
    participant R as ReservationRepository
    participant U as UserService
    participant D as Reservation
    participant H as ReservationHistoryRepository
    participant N as NotificationService
    Caller->>S: approve(id, actor, request) [Spring transaction]
    S->>S: check identity, TEACHER and input
    Note over S,R: Invalid input ends before repository reads.
    S->>R: findById(id)
    R-->>S: Optional(Reservation)
    S->>U: get(actor.id)
    U-->>S: AppUser
    S->>S: check ownership and PENDING
    alt foreign owner / invalid state
        S-->>Caller: ApiException 403 / 409; no writes
    else owner approves PENDING
        S->>D: confirm()
        S->>H: save(ReservationHistory)
        S->>N: create(student, RESERVATION_APPROVED, ...)
        Note over S,N: Propagate technical errors. Spring rolls back the transaction.
        S-->>Caller: ReservationResponse after successful commit
    end

D1–D3 imply rejection tests for invalid input, unauthorized actors and invalid states. D4–D5 require successful transition, correct history actor and correct notification recipient. D6 requires error propagation and atomic persistence verification.
The evidence table below links each decision to a test and explains the chosen test level. Unit tests replace database dependencies with mocks and cannot prove database rollback.

Two integration tests cover history failure and notification failure. They are implemented in ReservationApprovalPersistenceTests, alongside a positive commit check. Commit a PENDING fixture, call the service through Spring transaction support, and cause the relevant write to fail. In a new transaction verify PENDING, no confirmedAt, and unchanged history/notification counts. Automatic rollback of the test itself must not be mistaken for evidence of service rollback.
Getters, simple response mapping, exact notification wording and framework annotation syntax remain in code. The meaning of the transaction boundary is part of this design.
One service owns the rules. A separate policy class should be considered if distinct approval strategies need to be separated.
Revision: 2026-10-19. Unit: reservation approval, OP-05. The design above defines intended behavior; this evidence records verification and remaining work.

We compared the design with the C05 assignment, C02 requirements and current source files. Ownership was clarified: ReservationService decides approval; UserService only loads the user. The follow-up implementation added three integration cases in ReservationApprovalPersistenceTests. No further production change was needed; the tests verified the existing transaction behavior.
ReservationApprovalDesignTests contains 12 cases. The service and entities are real; repositories, UserService and NotificationService are mocks. This suite runs without Spring context or HTTP.

blocks.content: Level rationale 1: missingActorIsRejectedBeforeReadingReservation is a unit test of the public service contract. It protects non-HTTP callers too; an HTTP filter test alone cannot establish the order inside the service. The repository mock proves that no read occurred.

Level rationale 2: ownerApprovesWithCorrectAuditAndStudentNotification is a unit test with mocked boundaries. It verifies decision ownership, entity transition and the actual history content. A database is unnecessary for these decisions, but the test does not prove commit. ReflectionTestUtils inspects private history data without introducing production getters solely for testing.
Level rationale 3: notificationFailurePropagatesWithoutSuccessResponse verifies error propagation without a Spring proxy. Actual rollback requires an integration test against PostgreSQL.

Requires Java 21 and local PostgreSQL on localhost:5432 with the project defaults. The restricted environment blocked the database connection; successful runs used approved access outside it.

Integration tests create a random c05_test_… schema, apply real Flyway migrations and remove the schema afterwards. Fixtures are committed before calling the service. Tests do not run inside automatically rolled-back test transactions. Verification reads SQL in a fresh transaction.

Spies inject RuntimeException after flushing real database writes. The history test persists and flushes the changed reservation and audit record. The notification test calls the real create method and flushes all three writes. After failure, fresh SQL reads must show the original PENDING, null confirmedAt and unchanged history/notification counts. The positive test checks commit and correct actor/recipient. This does not simulate connection loss or concurrency.

Reports for all four classes are generated in backend/target/surefire-reports/ and are not versioned. The earlier 22-test run covered selected suites without database verification; 26 is the current complete result.

blocks.content: One approval strategy currently exists, so rules remain in one service. A separate policy class is unnecessary for this scope. The diagram shows repository interfaces and service dependencies.

items: Concurrent approvals are not serialized by locking or entity versioning and may create duplicate history/notifications. A sequential 409 test does not test concurrency.
Rollback is now verified against PostgreSQL for injected RuntimeExceptions after database writes. Connection loss and other failure types are outside this test scope.
Reservation.confirm() relies on service checks. Any new caller must respect the same contract.
